text: This app is good for all those who either want to start a new habit, or want to give up any bad habit. If seen in this way, then this app can prove to be very helpful in making us a good person in the true sense, because in this these habits can be easily tracked. There are three types of options available to track any habit in this: 1. ✔️ Track specific amount 2. ➕ Track specific time 3. ▶️Track your do's or don'ts 🔸Any habit has to be ☑️ Build, or 🚫 Quit. Or to 📊 simply track both of them and see its 📈 tracking progress, all this is possible with the help of all the above three options. ​ 🔹All Habits can be divided into different tags. Which can be easily accessed later in Habit windows by pressing on the filter icon. ​ ​ 🔹All these habits can also be rearranged again. 🔸Habits are in two types of structure. One grid and the other list. Habits structure can be changed from grid to list or list to grid by going to setting. ​ 🔹Habit windows have a weekly calendar view. Which saves us from unnecessary distractions. The statistics view of the individual habit is available in the following forms - [i.] Current or Highest streak (with more informations) [ii.] Success rate (%) [iii.] Frequency (Months Vs Days of the week) [iv.] History ( By Day, Week, Month, Year) [v.] Completions [vi.] Activity​ (calender) etc. Whereas the collective statistics of whole habits is also available, which we get to see in these forms - [i.] Streaks (Current streak & Highest streak) [ii.] Stats (Important informations) [iii.] Frequency (Months Vs Days of the week) [iv.] Activity (calender) Despite all this, it is also easy to make a to-do list in it. ⚪️In this, the tasks can be rearranged. ⚪️Also, these tasks can also be tagged in a different list. ⚪️Any important tasks can also be ST☆RRED. Notification - In this, there is a notification of a reminder of a to-do list, or a notification of a habit to be tracked for a specific time. The good thing is, "Timer still going notification" is available in the setting, with the help of which when any ongoing activities will end, it is known only after reading it from the notification shade. Widget - Individual widgets can be created for all individual habits. Its UI is also cool and great, which comes with dark & Light theme. The opening view of the app is also good. The icon of the app is also minimal. There are other good features, which can be known only after using it. Thank you! text: I bought a lifetime subscription to this because I can see it WILL be an amazing habit tracker, but I don't think it's quite there yet. My biggest takeaway is that Timecap has really creative developers looking to shake things up, which is GREAT given how dull and unimaginative these apps have become in recent years, but the boundary pushing does mean things aren't always as intuitive as they could be. The interface is interesting. It is in fact very customizable, and there are things I like about it (e.g., the overall Stats page), but again, it's not always intuitive. Sometimes you have to go to unexpected places to do basic things, like add notifications, sort habits, or create categories ("tags" in Timecap lingo). I'm not sure I believe this is the ideal interface for seeing personal progress, either. There's a reason "don't break the chain" visualizations exist. Timecap has those, actually, but you have to tap on each individual task to see the stats for that goal, which isn't as simple as seeing the current week's progress on a goal at a glance. Overall, I'd like to see Timecap keep its originality (and even quirky placement of features), but also maybe add in some of the traditional at-a-glance visualizations seen in other trackers. Cutting down on taps/clicks would be good. Best of both worlds. Finally, there are a few features I'd like to see that Timecap isn't so much missing as they are features most all habit trackers are missing. I love that Timecap recognizes you may want goals, limits, or timed activities, but I wish it and other habit trackers understood sometimes tracking isn't about completion or necessarily a matter of counting. A tracked habit might be more of a yes/no/maybe, good/okay/bad, dined in/dined out, etc. I'd love to see customizable terms here, with a way for users to dictate whether one term has a positive, neutral, or negative connotation to it. I'm enough of a designer/dev myself to know it's a big development ask, but I've been looking for an app to do this for years, and with Timecap aiming to be the "most customizable" tracker I'm hoping creative features like this or similar ones are in the pipeline. So far, I've not found a habit tracker that is quite what I want or need (and no, spreadsheets aren't an option!), but I really like that Timecap is out here trying to be different. This is not just another copy of an open source tracker using the same, tired ideas. I'm looking forward to seeing what they come up with in the future.
